quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
How much time passes between drinks

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol content depends on how much alcohol you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Food slows alcohol absorption but cannot prevent intoxication if you drink too much.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: The space needed to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren behind you. You should:

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop
Speed up to get out of the way

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, reduce your speed and safely pull over to the side of the road. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles

questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near their rear that cannot be seen in their side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive at the maximum posted speed limit
Drive closely behind the vehicle in front of you

questions.explanation: When rain reduces visibility, reduce your speed. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see your vehicle. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull off the road and stop until the rain lets up.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas
Do not immediately use your brakes
Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road

questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the gas and do not immediately apply the brakes. Gradually slow down before gently applying the brakes and pulling off the side of the road.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop
Give the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the road
Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room
Turn on your high beam headlights to make sure the other vehicle sees you

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the road
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give vehicles traveling in the opposite direction at least one-half of the road. Both vehicles need adequate space to safely pass each other.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means the road ahead has a series of turns or curves.

questions.question: A sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph" means:

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone
You should reduce your speed to 35 mph only during poor weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers they must slow down. The new speed limit starts at the sign.

questions.question: Driving at night is:
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see in the dark, headlight glare can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Stop only if other cars are approaching.

questions.explanation: This sign shows where bicycles cross or ride beside the road. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles are likely present.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never stay in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or back so the driver can see you.

questions.question: What lights must you use when driving in rain?
questions.explanation: In rainy conditions, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: How far ahead should you look to avoid sudden braking or turns?
questions.explanation: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle to avoid sudden braking or turns. This gives drivers behind you time to react to your movements.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Excessive speed under the driving conditions

questions.explanation: Speeding, inattention, and following too closely all cause accidents. Not paying attention can lead to crashes. Following too close causes most rear-end collisions.

questions.question: When a traffic light has been green for a long time, what should you do?

options.text: Prepare for the light to turn yellow.
Speed up to beat a red light.
Assume the light will stay green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare for the light to turn yellow.
questions.explanation: A light that has been green for a long time may change to yellow or red soon. Slow down and be ready for the light to change.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in their driveways with their cars running.

questions.explanation: Each quick stop uses fuel to speed back up. Looking ahead and slowing gradually helps you avoid sudden braking and saves gas.

questions.question: When should you use your parking brake?

options.text: Only when you park on a hill
Only when you're parked on a busy street
Only when you're parked in a parking lot

questions.explanation: Use your parking brake every time you park. It does not matter if the terrain is flat or hilly, or if your car is an automatic or manual.

questions.question: When may you drive above the speed limit?

options.text: When there is no police officer present.
When traffic around you is driving above the speed limit.
When you are in a hurry.

questions.explanation: Never drive above the speed limit. Obeying speed limits gives you time to change lanes, slow down, or stop if something unexpected happens.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. Solid white lines should not be crossed. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic going opposite directions.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is one who:

options.text: Looks at things off the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while having a conversation and driving.
Only watches the vehicle in front of them.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by looking at passengers, searching for items in your vehicle, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming while driving. Keep scanning the road, check your mirrors regularly, and look at your instrument panel often. These safe habits will help you stay focused as a driver.

questions.question: What can be hazardous when driving in autumn?

options.text: Rain and mist on the road

questions.explanation: Wet leaves create slippery and dangerous driving conditions. Daylight saving time ends, which means less visibility and less safe driving conditions. Slow down on slick roads and increase your distance from other cars when rain or mist appears. Even a small amount of water mixed with oil and grease on the road can make it slippery.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how well you can stop. You must slow down when roads are in poor condition to keep control of your vehicle. Driving too fast on slippery roads puts you at risk if you need to stop suddenly.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, other drivers must allow for:

options.text: The longer distance large vehicles need to stop.
The shorter distance large vehicles need to stop.
The less noise large vehicles make.
The faster speed of large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer distance large vehicles need to stop.
questions.explanation: When driving near large trucks, other drivers must allow for the longer distance these vehicles need to stop. Drivers of smaller vehicles should stay where the truck driver can see them and where their view is not blocked by the truck.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Circular signs warn of railroad crossings. This sign tells drivers they are approaching a railroad crossing and should watch for trains.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Do not need more room to turn than cars.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the rear. Do not stay in these areas. Because of their size and weight, trucks need more space to turn and stop than cars.

questions.question: To make sure your physical condition does not make you drive unsafely, you should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular physical exams.
Know how any medicine affects your driving.
Drive only within your physical abilities.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition is important for safe driving. Drivers should know their physical limits and only drive when it is safe.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multi-lane intersection and oncoming traffic blocks your view. You should:

options.text: Speed up quickly when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane of oncoming traffic as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and you can turn safely.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Regulation signs control traffic speed and movement and show rules drivers must follow. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: The "No zone" is:

options.text: A term for the blind spots around a truck or bus.
A road with rules about car stereo volume.
A TV show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A term for the blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on each side, in the rear, and in front. Cars in these spots cannot be seen by the driver. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. You must come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: When should you use a three-point turnabout?

options.text: Only when the road is too narrow to make a U-turn and you cannot go around the block.
When driving on a one-lane, one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when the road is too narrow to make a U-turn and you cannot go around the block.
questions.explanation: A three-point turnabout is difficult and dangerous. Use it only when the road is too narrow for a safe U-turn and you cannot go around the block. Only use this turn on a two-lane road.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: No less safe than driving under any other conditions.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely risky. It endangers you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers. Paying full attention to the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: Refusing to take an alcohol analysis test:

options.text: Is your right and will have no negative consequences.
Will result in one night in jail.

questions.explanation: When you drive in Louisiana, you automatically agree to an alcohol analysis test if an officer requests it. If you refuse the test, your license will be suspended for 365 days on a first offense or 730 days on a second or later offense.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
If you are both on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are both on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop while the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is out.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for nearby police cars.

questions.explanation: You may turn right or left at a green light unless a sign says otherwise. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass other vehicles in your direction.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Drive with your flashers turned on.
Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, move toward the edge of the road and stop.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Blow your horn to warn cars you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.
